description: Two-component, flexible cementitious mortar for waterproofing concrete surfaces subject to both positive and negative water pressure
whereToUse: Waterproofing concrete and masonry structures subject to positive or negative hydrostatic pressure.
It is recommended for foundation walls, car-parks and underground environments, basins, channels and swimming pools.
Waterproofing underground car-parks, cellars, sunken swimming pools and basins and lift pits against the counter-pressure of water.
Waterproofing breeze-block walls pre-treated with a suitable MAPEI mortar.
notFor: Do not use Mapelastic Foundation for coatings with a high thickness (more than 2 mm per coat).
Do not apply Mapelastic Foundation at temperatures below +5°C.
Do not apply Mapelastic Foundation on substrates saturated with water (surfaces must dry off before application).
Do not add cement, aggregates or water to Mapelastic Foundation.
Protect from rain and water contact for the first 24 hours after application.

standards.value: Complies with the requirements of EN 1504-2 Standards, PI, MC and IR principles
Mapelastic Foundation fulfils all the main criteria for the EN 1504-9 Standards
W < 0,07 kg/m²·h0,5 Class W3 (low water permeability) according to EN 1062-1)
Sd < 3 m Class I (permeable to water vapour)

technicalData.label: Mixing ratio
technicalData.value: component A : component B = 2.2 : 1 (one 22 kg bag of component A with one 10 kg can of component B)

technicalData.label: Permissible application temperature
technicalData.value: room and substrate temperature from +5°C to +35°C

technicalData.label: Manual application
technicalData.value: Mapelastic Foundation must be applied with a roller or a trowel within 60 minutes of it being mixed in at least two coats, to give a final thickness of at least 2 mm.

technicalData.label: The second coat
technicalData.value: may be applied approximately 6 hours after the first coat

technicalData.label: Spray application
technicalData.value: The final thickness must be at least 2 mm. After applying the first layer, wait until it has cured (approximately 6 hours) and then apply a second layer.

Impermeability to water under pressure (1.5 bar) of negative lift expressed as water penetration

notes: Consumption is given for roller (1.65) and for spray (1.75 flat, 2.1 rough), all per mm thickness; trowel is a listed manual application method but has no consumption figure. Required build: at least two coats, final thickness at least 2 mm, and not more than 2 mm per coat (see notFor). Two different upper application temperatures are printed: 'from +5°C to +35°C' in the application table and 'from +5°C to +40°C' in the technical data; both are recorded. In the application table the row labelled 'Mixing time' reads 'approx. 60 min. (at +20°C)', which matches the pot life ('approx. 60 mins.') and the 'within 60 minutes of it being mixed' instruction rather than a mixing duration; the actual mixing instructions are about 3 minutes, a 2 minute rest, then up to 2 more minutes. The Layer thickness row points to a section 'Applying the mortar' that does not exist under that name (the sections are 'Manual application' and 'Spray application'). The characteristics text says it may be applied 'with a roller or by spray' while Manual application says 'with a roller or a trowel'. Mixing ratio is printed '2.2 : 1' in one table and '2,2 : 1' in another, and mix density as '1650 kg/m3', '1650 kg/m³' and '1.650' (kg/m³), i.e. mixed decimal/thousands notation. Component B is called a '10 kg can' in the mixing row and '10 kg tanks' under packaging. The EN 14891 class is printed 'CM01P' in the heading sentence and 'CM O1 P' in the table header. The EN 14891 results table is headed 'Product performance with reinforcement' (crack-bridging 2.0 mm at +23°C, 1,2 mm at -5°C) but the sheet names no reinforcement product, so those values are not in technicalData; the crack-bridging row recorded is the EN 1062-7 static value, whose label is trimmed because the table cells are interleaved in the extraction. Negative pressure resistance is stated as 'up to 1.5 atm (15 m column of water)' in the text and tested at 1.5 bar in the table.
